rules.title: Notice of tenants’ rights when ending occupancy
rules.requirement: Covered landlords and foreclosing owners must provide the Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources when starting eviction, declining lease renewal, or asking a tenant or former homeowner to leave, delivering it together with the applicable termination notice. This is a notification requirement and does not establish permissible grounds for eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston, including purchasers of property out of foreclosure or from a bank or mortgage lender asking former owners or tenants to leave. Excludes residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, and residences in a nonprofit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a nonprofit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rules.citation: Housing Stability Notification Act, Sec. 10-11.7; Tenant FAQs, questions 1, 4 and 5
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of
Boston in October 2020 that requires any landlord planning to end a tenancy
agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.
The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must also be delivered to any tenant
that is asked to leave a property. For example, if someone is purchasing a property
out of foreclosure, or from a bank or a mortgage lender, they must provide this
Notice to the former owners of the property, or any tenants that live in the
property.

rules.title: HSNA rights cannot be waived or limited by agreement
rules.requirement: HSNA requirements cannot be waived; any lease, contract or other agreement term purporting to waive or limit a tenant’s or former homeowner’s substantive or procedural rights under the ordinance is contrary to public policy, unenforceable and void.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to agreement terms affecting HSNA rights of tenants or former homeowners where a landlord or foreclosing owner intends to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston. Excludes residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, and residences in a nonprofit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a nonprofit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rules.citation: Housing Stability Notification Act, Sec. 10-11.7; Tenant FAQs, questions 5 and 6
rules.quoted_span:
No. The requirements of this Ordinance may not be waived, and any term of any
lease, contract, or other agreement that purports to waive or limit a tenant’s or
former homeowner’s substantive or procedural rights under this Ordinance are
contrary to public policy, unenforceable, and void.

review.issue: All three rules require execution review because the supplied vocabulary cannot completely express the covered landlord/foreclosing-owner roles, termination triggers, post-foreclosure occupancy and precise facility exceptions. Their coverage is preserved as prose.
review.quoted_span:
The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a
tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
The only exempt properties are residences:
1. in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility;  and
2. in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term
treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance
abuse.

review.issue: The source expressly supplies November 6, 2020 as the effective date; its separate October 2020 passage date is not used as the effective date.
review.quoted_span: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.

review.issue: Separately located enforcement provisions state that, unless otherwise provided, a person or entity violating the ordinance receives a warning for the first offense and a $300-per-day fine for second and subsequent offenses, enforced by ISD. These sanctions are preserved here because the individual rule quotations do not contain them; the source does not specify additional per-tenant or per-notice counting.
review.quoted_span:
Unless otherwise provided, a person or entity violating any provisions of this 
Ordinance shall be punishable by a warning or fine in accordance with the 
provisions of City of Boston Ordinances and/or Boston City Charter, shown below. 
Housing Stability Notification Act (Sec. 10-11.7) 
Enforcement Entity: Inspectional Services Department 
1st Offense: Warning 
2nd and Subsequent Offenses: $300 per day

review.issue: The described tenant reporting route requires reporting to FHE, submitting requested information online or by mail, written proof of tenancy, a Notice to Quit or Court Complaint, and landlord or property-manager contact information. The FAQ conditions the described ticket issuance on missing required information and proper reporting; it does not establish a private damages action.
review.quoted_span:
Violations of the HSNA are investigated by the Office of Fair Housing and Equity
(FHE) and enforced by the Inspectional Services Department (ISD). ISD will issue a
ticket to your landlord if the required information is not provided to you and you
properly report the violation.
In order for ISD to issue a ticket, you will need to do the following: 

Housing Stability Notification Act 
Frequently Asked Questions for Tenants 
3 
1. Call FHE at 617-635-2500 and explain that you are calling to report a
violation of the new Housing Stability Notification Act. You can also call 311
and ask for FHE.
2. FHE may direct you to submit your information through an online intake
form available on FHE’s website: boston.gov/departments/fair-housing-
and-equity. If you are unable to use the online form, you may submit any
required documentation through the mail to the following address:
City of Boston 
Office of Fair Housing and Equity 
1 City Hall Square, Rm. 966 
Boston, MA 02201 
3. Provide FHE with written proof of your tenancy such as your lease, rent
receipts, or your name on a notice to quit or court complaint (other items
proving your tenancy may be accepted).
4. Provide FHE with a copy of the Notice to Quit or Court Complaint, as well as
your landlord or property manager’s contact information.

review.issue: The source expressly limits the effect of an HSNA violation: it does not halt eviction. The extracted procedural rules must not be evaluated as a universal just-cause requirement or automatic eviction stay.
review.quoted_span: If a landlord violates the HSNA, it DOES NOT halt the eviction process.
